messages:
sarah_cs: heads up — after last night's crm hygiene sweep some accounts show a sudden health_score drop. noticing a spike in 'missing_onboard_step' and 'last_activity_null' tags. did the playbook mapping get updated?

mike_ops: saw that in alerts too. i didn't touch the mapping rules this morning. which sweep run id?

sarah_cs: run id 2023-11-24-03h (nightly-hygiene). quick snippet from the audit: `update_playbook_ruleset('contact_merge_v2')` shows up in the logs around the same time.

anya_data: ping — i pulled a diff between pre/post hygiene snapshots. main changes: we backfilled email_normalization fallback for ~4k contacts and cleared duplicate-touchpoint anchors. that caused a few accounts to lose "last_activity" because touchpoints were re-assigned to canonical contacts.

anya_data: recommend two mitigations: 1) add a soft-backfill flag so playbooks don't clear last_activity when reassigning; 2) run a quick eval to see how healthscore formula responds. i sampled 500 affected accounts — median health_score dropped ~18 pts.

sarah_cs: 18 pts is huge. can we gate the sweep with a canary for high ARR accounts first? we can't risk renewals. @mike_ops can you add gating?

mike_ops: yes. i can add a canary toggle in playbook runner and limit to accounts with ARR > 50k for the next run. also can run the hygiene in dry-run mode and emit delta CSV.

ezra_ml: also suggest adding a calibration checkpoint in healthscorer: preserve `last_activity` if new touchpoint assignment is only metadata-level (email normalization) vs true event removal. we can add a lightweight rule: `if touchpoint_count_change < 0.1*prior_count then preserve_last_activity` — simple heuristic.

anya_data: here's the SQL i used for sampling — feel free to reuse:
```sql
SELECT account_id, prev_health_score, post_health_score, prior_touchpoint_count, new_touchpoint_count
FROM hygiene_audit
WHERE run_id = '2023-11-24-03h' AND prior_touchpoint_count > 0
ORDER BY ABS(prev_health_score - post_health_score) DESC
LIMIT 500;
```

mike_ops: copying that. i'll schedule a dry run with canary for ARR>50k and attach the delta CSV to this thread. ETA 45m.

sarah_cs: awesome. please also include a list of accounts flagged as renewal-risk by the post-run healthscore so cs team can reach out proactively.

mike_ops: will do. tagging the run: `hygiene-dryrun-canary-20231124`. launching now. @deploy-bot can you create the run artifact? :rocket:

deploy-bot: Run created: hygiene-dryrun-canary-20231124. Dry-run in progress. Artifacts will appear in S3: s3://redwood-hygiene/audit/hygiene-dryrun-canary-20231124.csv

mike_ops: dry-run done. attaching summary: affected_accounts=412, median_health_drop=17.8, renewal_risk_count=23. uploading CSV to the s3 path above.

sarah_cs: thanks. i'll open a short outreach queue for the 23 high-risk accounts — tagging @anya_data to validate the list before outreach.

anya_data: validating now, will confirm in 15m. preliminary pass: 19/23 look correct, 4 are false positives (recently reclassified as churned). i'll mark them and update the CSV.

ezra_ml: once validated we should add an automated safeguard: playbook automation should include a pre-hook that checks for >10% median health drop and pauses the run for manual review. i can PR a simple rule into the runner.

mike_ops: agreed. i'll accept the PR and make it feature-flagged. small ops note: make sure the flag defaults to off for small sweeps to avoid noise.

sarah_cs: perfect. documented next steps: 1) @anya_data finalize validated CSV; 2) @mike_ops merge canary gating + PR; 3) @ezra_ml add pre-hook alert rule; 4) cs team outreach for confirmed renewal-risk accounts. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
